images.title: One area, two heights
images.purpose: Show that the same triangle has one area whichever base and height pair is used, so a missing height can be found.
images.composition: One triangle with two dashed altitudes in two colours, the known pair and the unknown pair.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, the main figure large and centred with generous empty margins on all sides, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills, nothing else in the frame. A triangle ABC with corners B (0,0), C (5,0), A (2.35,3), so BC = 5, the height from A is 3 and AC = 4. Triangle filled very light grey. Dashed #0072B2 altitude AX from A straight down to X (2.35,0) with a right angle mark at X. Dashed #E69F00 altitude BY from B to Y (2.81,2.48) on side AC, perpendicular to AC, right angle mark at Y; Y is close to A, and BY runs close to side AB but is a separate dashed line. Side BC drawn in #0072B2, side AC drawn in #E69F00. Vertex letters 'A', 'B', 'C' at the corners. Labels kept away from A: 'BC = 5' under BC, 'AX = 3' to the right of the midpoint of AX, 'AC = 4' outside the triangle beside AC, 'BY = 3.75' at the midpoint of BY inside the triangle. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.description: Show that the same triangle has one area whichever base and height pair is used, so a missing height can be found.

images.teaching_notes: Area 7.5 square units from either pair; colour pairs each base with its own height.

image_decisions.why: Seeing both altitudes on one triangle is the idea: one area, two base and height pairs.
